svg.text: a small command-line notes tool, three tasks on its roadmap
the roadmap is a plain file in the repo; nothing here was typed for the picture

g.text: you
you: what's next?
Foreman
Two tasks are ready to go — neither is blocked, and nothing else is in flight.
Which task next?
1. Save notes to a file so they survive a restart (001) — (Recommended) Right now notes
only live in memory, so closing the terminal wipes everything; this makes the tool
usable past a single sitting. It leads because one other task is waiting behind it.
2. Add a --due flag to add (002) — People are typing dates into the note text by hand,
so nothing can sort or warn by date. It's just the oldest other ready task; nothing
is waiting on it.
You can also tell me something else you'd rather work on. Once you pick, I'll ask how
you want to run it (here as one task, split by check, a background agent, or copied to
your clipboard) — feel free to answer both at once.
you
you: 1. Copy the prompt to my clipboard.
Foreman
Task 001 — Save notes to a file so they survive a restart. Right now the notes tool
keeps everything in memory, so quitting the terminal throws away every note you took.
This makes the store write itself to a JSON file in your home directory whenever it
changes and read it back at startup, without touching any of the CLI's commands or
output.
…and on. 165 words in all.
you
you, in a fresh session:
<task_context>
You are a Node.js developer working on a small command-line notes tool.
Your goal is Notes added in one run of the CLI are still there in the next run,
because the store now persists itself to a JSON file in the user's home
directory and reads it back on start.
</task_context>
<relevant_files>
src/store.js — nextId (5), notes (6), add (8), list (14), markDone (18), reset
test/store.test.js — assert (4), store (5)
Pattern: src/cli.js — build the new code the same way
</relevant_files>
